counterfactual_missing_items: history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
decisive_items: Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions without evidence of acute infarction.
Subsequent brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia.
Laboratory testing revealed a blood glucose level of 8.59 mmol/L (reference range, 3.9–6.1) and a hemoglobin A1c of 7.43% (4–6)
response.rationale: R2 uniquely integrates the diabetic history, elevated glucose/HbA1c, and bilateral striatal T1 hyperintensity on MRI with striatal hyperdensity on CT, which is pathognomonic for diabetic striatopathy. R1 and C1 capture only the movement disorder and imaging findings but miss the diabetic cause. R3 captures the diabetic history but misses the imaging findings.

rejected.why: Misses the diabetic cause; label is a symptom, not a diagnosis.
Redundant with R1; anatomy modifier is inaccurate (hemichorea is unilateral).
Misses the imaging findings that are pathognomonic for diabetic striatopathy.
